key_insight: A rate-transfer method turns finite-time Lyapunov bounds for an associated SDE into finite-time convergence rates for stochastic gradient algorithms.
engineering_relevance: This provides a calculus-based way to prove and predict convergence behavior for SGD-type optimizers, including new variants, without requiring a full bespoke discrete-time analysis.
method: Model the stochastic gradient method with an associated SDE.
Verify a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE using calculus.
Transfer the resulting finite-time Lyapunov estimate into a convergence-rate bound for the algorithm.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method recovers established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and extends to new algorithms via SDE-based calculus arguments.
watch_item: The approach depends on moment and smoothness conditions plus a suitable SDE approximation, so rate guarantees may be sensitive to modeling assumptions.
paper_title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
